source.title: Evaluating Material Flammability in Microgravity and Martian Gravity Compared to the NASA Standard Normal Gravity Test
source.authors: Olson, S. L. and Ferkul, P. V. (NASA Glenn Research Center)
source.verification: Values typed from the text layer and checked by eye against a render of PDF page 6.
source.lunarAndZeroGOrigin: The lunar-gravity and 0g rows come from the paper's reference 8: Ferkul, P. V. and Olson, S. L., 'Zero-Gravity Centrifuge Used for the Evaluation of Material Flammability in Lunar Gravity', Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer 25(3), 2011.

definitions.ULOI: Upward limiting oxygen index: oxygen at which a material passes the NASA-STD-6001 Test 1 burn-length criterion about half the time (1 g).
definitions.MOC: Maximum oxygen concentration that consistently results in self-extinguishment (1 g).
definitions.ULOI*: Reduced gravity: lowest oxygen at which the flame survived the full drop time.
definitions.MOC*: Reduced gravity: highest oxygen at which the flame self-extinguished during the drop.

limits: Drop-tower tests in NASA Glenn's Zero Gravity Facility with a centrifuge; about 5 s of reduced gravity per test (5.18 s drop).
Reduced-gravity limits (ULOI*, MOC*) are defined differently from the 1-g limits because of the short test time.
The 0g* tests used a 30 cm/s concurrent flow; Martian- and lunar-gravity tests used buoyant flow from the centrifuge.
Three thin materials only. Published outside NASA's PSI archive.
